title: Where the time goes, by schedule
xLabel: schedule (64 GPUs, 1 GB buffer, 50 GB/s NDR)
caption: Startup versus byte-transfer terms on the chapter's reference collective. The ring spends nearly nothing on latency at this size but the term is O(N) — at 1,024 ranks it dominates. The simple tree inverts the profile: few rounds, full-message hops. Hierarchical pays a middle path by keeping the slow hop parallel.

title: Advertised versus effective compression
caption: Headline ratios discounted by what actually ships. Top-k 0.1% advertises 1,000× and delivers ~500× once index bytes count; INT8 with block-128 scales reaches 3.88× of its 4× ceiling; 1-bit Adam's end-to-end gain is ~5× because warmup runs uncompressed. Against a BF16 baseline every ratio halves.
